title: From One Chatbot to a Team of Agents
subtitle: How Google ADK turns prototypes into production teams
intro: You asked one AI to do everything and it got confused. What if you gave it a team with a clear org chart instead?
takeaway: Production agents work as a team: deterministic code handles the predictable paths, AI handles the judgment calls.

sections.heading: Everyday analogy: the restaurant kitchen
sections.body:
Think of a restaurant kitchen. One cook doing everything is slow and messy.

A real kitchen has stations: one chops, one grills, one plates. A ticket (graph) tells each dish where to go next.

Google's ADK builds AI the same way: small specialist agents linked by a graph-based workflow, not one giant prompt. That leads to why this exists.

sections.heading: Why does this exist?: reliable logic plus smart reasoning
sections.body:
A production agent needs two things. Deterministic logic means code that always follows the same rule, like check inventory first. LLM reasoning means the AI can adapt and decide in open-ended situations.

ADK lets you weave them together and orchestrate agents via graphs with explicit execution paths. You also get structured context management, so each agent only sees what it needs.

It is open-source and model-agnostic, available in Python, TypeScript, Go, Java and Kotlin. But even a good kitchen can fail.

sections.heading: What can go wrong: when the team breaks down
sections.body:
If your graph is too complex, tasks loop or stall and latency spikes.

If context is managed poorly, agents lose memory or leak private data to the wrong station.

If you rely only on AI reasoning with no deterministic checks, outcomes become unpredictable and hard to debug at enterprise scale.

steps.narration: User sends a task that is too complex for one prompt.
Orchestrator graph splits work and sets explicit paths.
Structured context shares only needed memory.
ADK deploys team across models and languages.

quiz.q: What does ADK mainly help you build?
quiz.why: ADK is for building, debugging and deploying reliable multi-agent systems with graph-based orchestration.

quiz.q: What fails first if usage grows 100x without good design?
options: Context overload, loops, and unpredictable latency
quiz.why: At scale, poor context management and overly complex graphs cause stalls, leaks, and latency.

quiz.q: What does hybrid deterministic + AI reasoning mean?
options: Weave predictable code paths with adaptive AI decisions
quiz.why: ADK weaves deterministic code for predictable outcomes with LLM reasoning for adaptability.
